piece.title: String Quartet No.12 in F major, Op.96 (“American”)
piece.why: Pretty and clear, then a handoff: Violin I sings the theme, then the cello takes it over while Violin I drops to the repeated-note accompaniment on top.

plan.summary: As written (no arranging): the original parts are handed out unchanged. The source parts in score order (Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Violoncello) are paired with the players sorted from highest to lowest range center (the midpoint of each player's sounding range): Violin 1 → Flute; Violin 2 → Clarinet in B♭; Viola → Alto Sax in E♭; Violoncello → Bassoon. No octave shifts, no chord changes beyond what a one-note instrument requires (a wind or brass player plays the top note of a double stop or chord), and no repair: a note outside a player's range stays where it is and is marked with an x notehead.
